resources.string:
Balance shows how power is split between left and right, using the Karoo’s 3-second average. You can set a warning for the deviation from 50/50 in percentage points.

PS (pedal smoothness) describes how evenly power is applied through one pedal revolution. TE (torque effectiveness) compares net torque with the positive torque during that revolution. SRM lists 10–40% for PS and 60–100% for TE as typical readings. Compare readings at similar power and cadence. A study found that actively pulling up increased mechanical effectiveness while reducing efficiency.

A compatible power meter must send these metrics to the Karoo, typically over ANT+. Performance averages both PS readings or marks a single reading L or R. Dynamics shows PS and TE per side. A dash indicates missing data.
SRM · Typical PS and TE readings

The Karoo provides the ride’s NP, IF, TSS and estimated calories from power. NP (normalized power) estimates the steady power that would have a similar physiological cost to a ride with varying power. IF (intensity factor) divides NP by your functional threshold power (FTP). TSS (training stress score) combines intensity and duration into an estimate of ride load. The kcal value estimates energy expenditure from measured power.

A ride best is the highest average power over the selected duration in elapsed time. Coasting, manual pauses and Auto Pause count as zero watts. For example, four minutes at 250 W and one minute stopped average 200 W over five minutes. When valid power readings resume after a dropout, the missing seconds also count as zero watts. An uploaded power curve can differ if the service corrects the sensor data or the recording used a different power source.\n\nIntervals.icu provides the comparison values. In the table, green marks a new 42-day best and purple a new all-time best. Purple takes priority if both are beaten.

Critical power (CP) is the threshold in the power–duration model. W′ is the finite amount of work you can do above it, measured in kilojoules. kEtape uses your manual CP and W′ or takes cycling FTP and W′ from Intervals.icu, using FTP as the reference power. For an indoor ride, kEtape uses your indoor FTP if it is set.

Réserve uses the differential W′ balance model described by Skiba and Clarke. The estimated reserve falls above the reference power and recovers below it. Balance shows what remains and estimates time to empty or to 90% at the current effort. Available Power adds remaining W′ (in joules) divided by the duration (in seconds) to the reference power. Insights summarizes the lowest and average reserve, work expended above the reference and time above it.

These are pacing estimates. A warning symbol marks uncertain continuity after a restart.
W′ depletion and recovery · Skiba et al. (2012)

You can smooth the large reading for power, heart rate, speed and cadence using a rolling average. The smaller ride summaries come from the Karoo. Power and heart-rate colors follow your Karoo zones. Speed and distance follow the distance unit on your Karoo. Ascent and descent (↗ and ↘) use its separate elevation unit.
